key_insight: This paper introduces Bi-CFM, a bidirectional generative approach that can infer plausible initial conditions from final states in chaotic systems. It tackles the core challenge of chaos by learning distribution-to-distribution mappings rather than assuming a single deterministic reverse solution.
problem_solved: The paper addresses inverse problems in chaotic dynamics: recovering unknown initial conditions from observed final states. These problems are difficult because they are ill-posed, non-unique, unstable, and may involve chaotic behavior when run backward in time.
method: Uses Bidirectional Conditional Flow Matching (Bi-CFM) to learn mappings in both forward and reverse directions.
Models the stochastic nature of chaotic evolution by learning distributions of initial and final states instead of one-to-one trajectories.
Mitigates instability in inverse inference by conditioning on observed states and capturing multiple valid solutions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical framework for solving inverse problems where exact recovery is impossible or ambiguous. It could improve scientific machine learning applications in physics, forecasting, control, and system identification for chaotic systems.

paper_title: Solving Inverse Problems of Chaotic Systems with Bidirectional Conditional Flow Matching
paper_authors: Peiyan Hu, Jian Zhang, Jiashu Pan, Ruiqi Feng, Tao Zhang
